title: Verizon Has Mobile Strength but Faces Legacy Pressure
text:

https://www.barrons.com/articles/verizon-stock-earnings-mobile-telecom-1538687770 Verizon Has Mobile Strength but Faces Legacy Pressure By Oct. 4, 2018 5:17 p.m. ET Order Reprints Agence France-Presse/Getty Images Text size
Verizon Communications (VZ) led the Dow Jones Industrial Average Thursday, with its shares climbing 1.3% to $55.02 as a handful of analysts weighed in on the company’s upcoming earnings report.
Instinet ’s Jeffrey Kvaal , who rates Verizon at Buy with a $65 price target, writes that the carrier looks positioned to report better-than-expected postpaid subscriber numbers when it delivers third-quarter results on Oct. 23. That would mark the fifth straight beat on the postpaid metric, fueled by weakness at Sprint (S) but overall strong trends in the wireless business.
Kvaal highlights strength from an Apple (AAPL) product, but not the obvious one. The Apple Watch Series 4 is “doing very well,” according to his channel checks. “We believe the Series 4 to be extremely profitable given the margins on a monthly [average revenue per user] of $10,” he writes.
Wells Fargo analyst Jennifer Fritzsche , who rates the company at Outperform with a $58 price target, comments that the wireless market is “competitive, but relatively rational” these days. She points to Verizon’s buy-one-get-one iPhone offer, which applies to phones above $700 and is just for customers who add a new line.
The view is more downbeat for Verizon’s wireline business, however. Instinet’s Kvaal writes that “ongoing pressure from legacy technologies, increasing content costs, and price compression” will likely continue to weigh on margins.
Fritzsche takes a similar view, writing that she expects those trends to continue in the immediate term until Verizon is able to scale its 5G efforts.
“We would note the tone around enterprise remains especially weak,” she adds.
Fritzsche sees further opportunities for the company to cut costs given that it announced early this week a voluntary severance package affecting about 25% of its employees.
Verizon shares are up 10% over the past year and have outperformed both Sprint and AT&T (T) shares. T-Mobile US shares have gained 12% over that time, but all four carriers have underperformed the broad market.
